I found LeCun's words word for word in the Collège de France press kit. The claim is out: in February 2016 he held no qualifying role, and "a few decades" doesn't count as a date anyway.

**1. The page.** The PDF opened. It is a 13-page press kit headed "Communiqué de presse Février 2016", for his Collège de France lecture series. His inaugural lecture was on 4 February 2016. The quote is in an essay signed in the page footer as "Yann LeCun – Titulaire de la chaire Informatique et Sciences numériques du Collège de France, Année académique 2015-2016". So these are his own written words, not a news report. The next sentence is as the search run said: "Mais c'est un futur lointain où l'on pourra donner de l'autonomie aux machines." The page gives no day for the essay itself, only February 2016.

**2. The rule.**
- **Part 1 (role) fails.** In February 2016 he was the founding director of Facebook AI Research. The press kit calls him "chercheur et directeur du laboratoire de recherche en intelligence artificielle de Facebook". That is a lab director, not a chief executive, founder-leader, chair or named chief scientist. He became Meta's Chief AI Scientist only around 2018. He is also signing here as a Collège de France chair-holder, not speaking for Facebook.
- **Part 3 (date) also fails.** "Dans quelques décennies" ("in a few decades") names no length. Under ruled reading 3, "a few years" is undated, and "a few decades" reads the same way. The "peut-être" ("perhaps") makes it softer still.
- **Not a repeat.** None of his recorded claim files covers 2016 or this point, so it isn't "recorded".

I've given part 1 as the failed part because it decides the matter first. A checker may want to log part 3 as a second, independent reason.
